issues.description: The helper method singFarmSongVerse has inconsistent visibility across artifacts. The UML in the problem statement marks singFarmSongVerse as private ("- singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void") and the template's Farm.java declares a private singFarmSongVerse (with the parameter commented out). The solution's Farm.java, however, implements singFarmSongVerse as protected. This visibility mismatch can confuse students about the intended access level (private vs protected) and whether the method should be callable from outside the class or by subclasses/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent. Either change the solution's singFarmSongVerse to private to match the UML/template (e.g., private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }), or update the UML and the template method declaration to protected and document the reason (e.g., to allow subclassing or test access). Also ensure the method signature includes the Animal parameter consistently in template and solution.
